$comment: Provenance record for the design content pack. Method: every file in the pack was byte-compared (md5) against the candidate upstream repositories named in runtime/agents/design-engineer.md, fetched from GitHub raw at the shas recorded under `sources`. Licenses were read from the upstream LICENSE files themselves (copied verbatim into packs/design/licenses/), not inferred from a README or from memory. HONESTY RULE: `provenance` is `verified` only when a byte-level or field-level comparison against a named upstream succeeded during this audit; `asserted` when the origin is documented in-repo but was not independently confirmed; `unknown` when neither holds. A license is never recorded unless it was read from an upstream LICENSE file or declared in the vendored file's own frontmatter. Where the audit could not establish something — most importantly the commit each subtree was originally vendored at — the field is null with a `nullReason`, rather than guessed. Paths are relative to packs/design/.

audit.method: md5 byte-comparison of every pack file against upstream raw.githubusercontent.com content, plus frontmatter field survey
audit.tooling: curl + md5sum; GitHub trees API for upstream layout
audit.limitation: Comparison is against each upstream's current default branch, not against the tree as it stood when this pack was vendored. Files recorded as `modified` may differ because of local edits, upstream drift since vendoring, or both; where the audit inspected the diff, the cause is stated.
audit.limitationScope: As of 2026-09-01 every vendored subtree is pinned. design-systems/ at e1c277c, craft/ at dceac12, design-skills/ at f631a09, workflow-skills/ at e1c277c. Local edits remain recorded per-subtree; the pin is the upstream commit to diff against, not a claim of byte-identity.

sources.supplies: prose doctrine only; no file redistributed, no code ported
sources.suppliesDetail: Three arguments from PHILOSOPHY.md, restated in our own words in craft/design-intent.md: (1) the prose is the specification and token values are context, not rendering instructions; (2) a specific reference carries more than a list of adjectives, because adjectives name a REGION of design space and a model outputs the centre of it; (3) negative constraints arrive for free when the reference is specific, so a long rambling don't-list is evidence the description was too vague to carry them. Paraphrased rather than quoted. Both projects are Apache-2.0, so a verbatim lift would have been permissible with attribution; paraphrase was chosen to avoid adding §4(b) modification-notice bookkeeping to craft/, a subtree that already carries an open licensing question (see openQuestions apache-notice-placement) and whose whole value rests on every other file being byte-identical to a different upstream.
sources.dissentNote: THIS UPSTREAM ARGUES AGAINST WORK THIS REPO HAS QUEUED, and the disagreement is recorded here rather than left in a craft file nobody re-reads — the same treatment given the picsum.photos conflict between open-design and stitch-skills. PHILOSOPHY.md states that token values serve as context and are NOT rendering instructions, and that token requirements in a specification are neither accepted nor recommended. the repository history task 33 proposes vendoring per-brand tokens.css for all 137 brands precisely so a brand stops being prose-only and becomes a checkable :root contract. That premise is what this upstream rejects.
sources.dissentDisposition: OPEN — recorded, not adjudicated, and task 33 is NOT blocked by it. The two positions are compatible for as long as a vendored :root contract is treated as a VERIFICATION SURFACE for gates and not as the brand's definition; they stop being compatible the moment an agent is pointed at tokens.css instead of DESIGN.md. Whoever actions task 33 should read craft/design-intent.md §1 first and record which of those two readings they are building. Note the objection comes from a THIRD PARTY: task 33 would vendor from nexu-io/open-design, not from this repo, so this is an outside argument against a design decision rather than two sources of the same bytes disagreeing — which is why it is filed as a dissent rather than a conflict.
sources.alsoEvaluated: This same repo's linter was evaluated and REJECTED as a dependency for scripts/lint-design-systems.mjs: it requires YAML front matter and returns NO_YAML_FOUND on 136 of our 137 files, and its CANONICAL_ORDER flags 79/137 for one systematic lineage difference. Two of its rules (contrast on declared pairs, canonical section order) were reimplemented against the shape our files actually have; no code was transliterated. See that script's header comment and the repository history.

(2) Three craft files — typography.md, color.md, anti-ai-slop.md — carry an inline '> Adapted from [refero_skill] (MIT)' blockquote. (3) refero_skill ships references/{typography,color,anti-ai-slop,motion,icons,copywriting,craft-details}.md, the same subject axis, at the same paths-by-topic. (4) Diffing refero's references/{anti-ai-slop,color,typography}.md against open-design's craft/ counterparts shows a heavy rewrite and condensation (378, 649, 827 diff lines respectively), not a copy — open-design's own copyright in the derived text is substantial. The chain is real; the bytes we hold are open-design's.

The README's blanket 'craft content is adapted from refero_skill' is broader than the per-file evidence supports; both licenses are shipped, so the conservative reading costs nothing.

sources.supplies: Factual token VALUES only, to two files: (1) design-systems/material/DESIGN.md, whose palette, typography, spacing, breakpoint and motion tokens were corrected against MUI's shipped defaults - see resolvedContentDefects id `material-design-system-misstates-its-own-brand`; (2) craft/layering.md, which cites MUI's zIndex ladder and its three elevation shadow alphas as reference values, the way animation-discipline.md cites Material 3 and Carbon motion tokens.
sources.whyValuesNotBytes: MUI is a React component library and this repository ships no React, so there is nothing here to vendor. What transfers is the numeric content of a design system that packs/design already names a brand file after. Values are facts about Material and are recorded with the file and symbol each was read from, so any of them can be re-checked at the pinned sha.
sources.m2NotM3Note: MUI implements Material 2, not Material 3, and its own source says so - createTransitions.js cites m2.material.io for both its easing and its duration tables, and createTypography.js cites m2.material.io for the type scale. Every value taken is therefore an M2 value. This is stated rather than smoothed over because craft/animation-discipline.md explicitly lints shipping the M2 easing curve under the name M3, and design-systems/material/DESIGN.md now carries that same warning inline. An M3 re-grounding of that file would be a separate piece of work against a different source.
sources.checkedAndRejected: colorManipulator.js getLuminance/getContrastRatio were compared against scripts/lint-design-systems.mjs and deliberately NOT adopted. Both implement the same WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula, but MUI truncates luminance with `.toFixed(3)` before taking the ratio, which can move a borderline pair across the 4.5:1 threshold. Our implementation does not truncate and is the more accurate of the two. Recorded so the comparison is not re-run as if it were an open question.

sources.deliberatelyNotTaken: The skill's reference palette. Its 8 light + 8 dark hex values were run through its own validator while craft/data-visualization.md was authored and they pass in both modes (worst adjacent CVD dE 9.1 light / 8.4 dark; worst adjacent normal-vision dE 19.6 light / 19.3 dark; first three slots clear the all-pairs floors in both modes). They are still not reproduced here, for two reasons. (1) Provenance: with no readable LICENSE, copying ~16 hex values would put unlicensed content into a pack whose entire value rests on every value being traceable to a license someone actually read. (2) Shape: craft/ states what holds regardless of brand and design-systems/*/DESIGN.md supplies values, so a fixed palette in a craft file is the wrong layer. The craft file carries the thresholds and the --series-N token contract instead, and a brand declares and validates its own palette against them.
sources.verificationNote: The threshold figures quoted in craft/data-visualization.md were re-derived by running the skill's own validator during authoring rather than copied from its prose, on the same principle the rest of this manifest applies: a number is recorded only when it was measured here.

vendoring.pinnedCommitSubject: fix(packaged): recover od:// after web sidecar exits (#6364)
vendoring.whyThisSha: Upstream HEAD at the time of vendoring, and NOT mid-refactor with respect to this subtree. The last commit to touch design-systems/ was ad5a7d6ba (2026-07-27), itself a full Revert of 340cbb9b9 'feat(web): add guided inspiration and deliverable workflow'; the revert restored the tree to exactly 049e1fa9b, byte-identical to its state at 6b90486c9 (2026-07-18). So design-systems/ has been unchanged for a week, the one recent churn is resolved rather than in flight, and 049e1fa9b is a settled state rather than a snapshot mid-series. vendoring.method: --filter=blob:none clone (retains every tree, so blob SHAs are readable without fetching content), then sha256 of every DESIGN.md against the pinned tree's counterpart.

That window (9ee2c19..483e00d, 57 commits sharing design-systems tree 0fdec161) was the best record obtainable while nothing in our files distinguished commits inside it. It is retained as history — it still explains why the record used to be a range, and it is still the ONLY record for workflow-skills/, which was not re-vendored.

detail.byteIdenticalScope: Against the PINNED commit e1c277c5, which was upstream HEAD when this figure was measured. 137 of the 150 open-design files are byte-identical; the remaining 13 are the local edits below. bmw-m is excluded from both figures because it does not come from open-design at all.
detail.modificationCause: TWO causes now, down from three. (1) Local de-branding, applied by commit d458c02 'Restructure into three top-level components; dedupe, de-brand, fix CI' — e.g. design-systems/voltagent replaces 'GitHub stars badge' with 'community badge'. Eight files: cal, dashboard, expo, framer, kami, ollama, replicate, voltagent. (2) Accessibility defect fix, 2026-08-03: four Schema-B files (bold, energetic, mono, pacman) shipped a declared Text/Surface pair below WCAG AA and had their Text token corrected — see resolvedContentDefects id declared-text-on-surface-contrast for the per-file values and reasoning. Recorded here rather than annotated in the files so the remaining bytes stay comparable to upstream. The THIRD cause this key used to carry — upstream drift since vendoring — is GONE as of the 2026-08-03 re-vendor: all seven drifted files were realigned to the pinned tree, so drift is no longer a reason any file here differs. (3) Brand-accuracy fix, 2026-08-14: design-systems/material/DESIGN.md declared tokens, fonts and a type scale that are not Material's - see resolvedContentDefects id `material-design-system-misstates-its-own-brand`. Corrected against mui/material-ui at 48c6663a. Same recording convention as cause (2): the values live here, not as an in-file annotation, so every untouched line stays comparable to upstream.
detail.reVendor2026-08-03: The subtree was re-vendored from a --filter=blob:none clone at the pinned sha. What happened, by class: 117 files were already byte-identical and were left alone; 7 files that differed ONLY by upstream drift (arc, canva, discord, duolingo, github, huggingface, openai) were realigned — each was a pure ADDITION of a '## 7. Usage Guardrails' section with no other line changed; 12 files carrying local edits were KEPT, verified line-by-line against the pinned tree first (upstream had changed nothing else in any of the 12 — identical line counts, differences confined to exactly the lines we edited, so there was no upstream content to merge around them); bmw-m was kept as-is because it is not an open-design file; and 14 brands upstream had added were brought in. Result: 137 -> 151 slugs, 117 -> 138 byte-identical, 19 -> 12 modifiedOrDrifted.

exceptions.note: Byte-identical to VoltAgent/awesome-design-md design-md/bmw-m/DESIGN.md except for one line: upstream `name: BMW-M-design-analysis` was changed to `name: BMW M`. This is the only file in design-systems/ with YAML frontmatter, and the only one that does not come from open-design; open-design ships its own, different bmw-m.
exceptions.reVendorDecision: KEPT as VoltAgent's at the 2026-08-03 re-vendor, deliberately, and this is the one place the three-way classification needed a human call. Mechanically, bmw-m falls into 'differs from the pinned open-design tree and is not in modifiedByUs', which is the bucket that otherwise means realign. It must NOT be realigned: the two files are different works, not two versions of one (ours 503 lines with YAML frontmatter, open-design's 246 lines in the standard prose schema; 589 diff lines). Overwriting ours with open-design's would swap the file's licence from MIT to Apache-2.0, void the `exceptions` record above, and discard the only YAML-frontmatter file in the subtree. Anyone re-running the classification should expect bmw-m in that bucket and exclude it before concluding the separation is wrong.

detail.differsOnlyByUpstreamDriftNote: EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION as of 2026-08-03, not by coincidence. This key previously held arc, canva, discord, duolingo, github, huggingface and openai — seven files that differed from upstream only because upstream moved on and we never took the update. All seven were realigned to the pinned tree during the re-vendor. Each turned out to be a pure addition of a '## 7. Usage Guardrails' section (3-4 bullets) at the end of the file with no other line touched, which is why realigning them was safe and why none of them needed a merge decision. Now that the subtree is pinned, this list should stay empty: any future non-empty value means someone edited a vendored file without recording it in modifiedByUs, or the pin moved without the tree being resynced.
detail.separationMethod: NOW TRIVIAL, because the subtree is pinned. Any file that differs from design-systems tree 049e1fa9b at commit e1c277c5 is our edit, and must appear in modifiedByUs. There is no longer an inference step and no longer a category of difference this manifest cannot attribute. bmw-m is the single documented exception and is not an open-design file at all (see exceptions above).
detail.separationMethodHistory: Before the pin, the two causes had to be told apart by matching every file against upstream HISTORY with a blob:none clone: files whose content matched SOME historical upstream state were upstream drift; files matching NO upstream state at any commit were our edits. Earlier still, the two could not be separated at all and all 15 differing files were recorded flatly as modified. That inference is what the pin replaces, and it is the substantive win of the 2026-08-03 re-vendor — openQuestions/vendoring-commits-unrecorded existed precisely because 'has this drifted?' could only be asked against a moving branch. The four contrast fixes (bold, energetic, mono, pacman) never needed the inference: they were recorded as our edits at the moment they were made, which is the convention every future local edit should follow — record the edit when you make it, do not leave it to be reconstructed.

subtrees.copyrightNote: The content is written as 'Design System Inspired by <brand>' — prose analysis of publicly observable visual language, not copied brand assets. That framing is upstream's, authored at nexu-io/open-design and VoltAgent/awesome-design-md; it was NOT clean-room reinterpretation performed in this repo. Everything here is a redistributed copy of upstream text. Brand names, wordmarks, and trademarks referenced in the prose remain the property of their respective owners and are used nominatively.
subtrees.correctionNote: An earlier internal description of this pack characterised design-systems/ as clean-room reinterpretation authored here. That is wrong: 138 of 151 files are byte-identical to upstream (117 of 137 when this note was first written). The correct characterisation is redistribution under Apache-2.0 (and MIT for bmw-m).

newBrands2026-08-03.generatorDefectCheck: All 14 were checked for the declared-Text-on-Surface defect that produced the bold/pacman/energetic/mono repairs, using the same declared-pair extraction scripts/lint-design-systems.mjs uses. NONE of the 14 carries a declared pair at all: not one has the Schema-B prose triplet ('Favor Primary (#…) for CTA emphasis' / 'Use Surface (#…) for large backgrounds' / 'Keep body copy on Text (#…) for legibility'). They are Schema-A and Schema-A-like files whose palettes are described in role prose rather than emitted by the Schema-B generator, so the defect's mechanism is not present. Zero repairs were needed and zero were applied — no new slug was added to modifiedByUs by this operation.

These 14 join the 80 pre-existing files that declare no pairing and are correctly not contrast-checked; the gate cannot speak to them either way. What was ruled out is specifically the upstream generator defect, which only manifests through the declared triplet.

Nothing read it — scripts/generate-design-catalog.mjs explicitly filtered it out. Verified before removal that it carried no information the directory tree does not: `slug` equals the directory name for all 57 entries, `name` equals the `name` field in the corresponding DESIGN.md frontmatter for all 57 entries (zero mismatches), and both paths are derivable from the slug. Fixing the paths would have made it correct but still unread, and would have broken byte-comparison against upstream — the one thing the file was actually good for. Its snapshot value is preserved above under `absentFromUpstreamHead` and `upstreamSize`.

files.note: It resolves a CONTRADICTION, not only a gap, and that is the part worth preserving. color.md caps visible --accent uses at 2 per screen; anti-ai-slop-rules.json fires `accent-overuse` at 6 uses of var(--accent) and `raw-hex` at 12 hexes outside :root; and a grep for --chart-N / --series-N / --cat-N across all 151 design-systems, 57 design-skills, 31 workflow-skills and craft/ returned ZERO hits. A six-series chart therefore had no legal route: reusing the accent tripped one rule, inventing hexes tripped another. The ruling is that series colour is an IDENTITY role and accent colour an ATTENTION role, so the accent cap counts accent uses and never applied to --series-N. color.md is neither edited nor contradicted; the fault was in what the pack failed to say.

subtrees.ruleTableNote: craft/anti-ai-slop-rules.json is authored here and is the only file in this subtree that draws on a second upstream. It encodes 18 mechanically checkable rules — 10 from nexu-io/open-design, 7 from google-labs-code/stitch-skills, 1 (invented-metric) combining both — as data, with a P0/P1/P2 ladder. It carries NO upstream code: open-design's enforcement lives in apps/daemon/src/lint-artifact.ts (Apache-2.0) and porting it would have pulled Apache-2.0 code into an MIT script. Rules-as-data keeps the licence boundary exactly where the pack boundary already is, and the rule set reviewable without touching the gate. Its `notAdopted` list records 15 upstream rules that were deliberately refused, each with the reason and, where triage informed the call, the hit count over this pack's 67 HTML files.

detail.lintDesignSystemsChange2026-08-03: The 2026-08-03 re-vendor required ONE change to lint-design-systems.mjs, recorded here because it was the only edit outside the vendored content and a reviewer should be able to judge it as gate-weakening or not. Three of the 14 incoming brands (totality-festival, urdu, wechat) failed the STRUCTURE check — never the contrast check — purely because they head equivalent sections with wording the synonym table did not know: 'Brand Identity', 'Spacing System', 'Component Styles', 'Motion & Animation', 'Brand Voice & Tone', 'Layout & Spacing', 'Spacing & Layout Grid', "Do's & Don'ts". Each was added to HEADING_ALIASES pointing at the slot the equivalent heading already used, and COLOR_H2 was widened to accept 'Color Palette' with an optional trailing parenthetical. NO schema was added, no threshold moved, and no contrast logic was touched. The alias table is the script's documented mechanism for exactly this — it already held 'component stylings', 'motion & interaction' and 'voice & brand' as synonyms of the same slots.
detail.lintDesignSystemsChangeWhyNotAWeakening: Two independent checks that it did not become a rubber stamp. (1) The three deliberately-malformed fixtures in evals/design-system-lint/ still fail: malformed-order still trips on Components-before-Color, and no-color-section still trips because 'Palette Notes' is deliberately still NOT matched by the widened COLOR_H2. The self-test runs on every invocation and reports 4 fixtures + 11 pattern cases, 0 problems. (2) No new SCHEMA was invented for a one-off file. totality-festival places Depth before Components, which looks like a third lineage but is not: bmw-m already ships that same order and already passed, because tokens absent from the schema being tried are treated as extras and it resolves against Schema B. Once 'Layout & Spacing' was aliased, totality-festival resolved the same way.
detail.lintDesignSystemsPreexistingBugFixed: Widening COLOR_H2 also fixed a latent inconsistency that predates this change: HEADING_ALIASES already mapped bare 'color palette' to the colour slot while COLOR_H2 did not match it, so a file using that heading would have been reported as having no colour section while its structure check passed. No file in the 137-slug corpus used that heading, so it never fired; two of the incoming 14 do.
detail.lintDesignSystemsNote: lint-design-systems.mjs is the only script in this pack that reads design-systems/ content and can fail on it. It is read-only by construction — every mutating fs entry point is replaced with a throwing stub before the first file is opened — because byte-comparability against upstream is what `separationMethod` depends on. It reimplements two rules from google-labs-code/design.md rather than taking that package as a dependency: that linter requires YAML front matter and returns NO_YAML_FOUND on 136 of our 137 files, and its CANONICAL_ORDER flags 79/137 for a single systematic lineage difference. No upstream code was transliterated; the script is MIT like the rest of scripts/.

openQuestions.question: Apache-2.0 §4(b) requires modified files to carry a notice of modification. This manifest and packs/design/README.md record the modified set centrally rather than annotating each modified file in place. Central notice is the common practice and keeps the vendored files byte-comparable against upstream, but a reviewer may prefer per-file headers.
openQuestions.decision: Central. No per-file headers were added at the re-vendor and none should be added without revisiting this entry. The reasoning that settles it is the same one that keeps packs/ out of Prettier: a per-file header would put a locally-authored line into every modified vendored file, and byte-comparability against the pinned tree is now the whole separation method (see subtrees[design-systems/].detail.separationMethod). Annotating the files would defeat the mechanism that identifies which files are annotated.
openQuestions.modifiedSetDerivation: 23 files across the pack carry a §4(b) obligation, all Apache-2.0 from nexu-io/open-design: 12 in design-systems/ (apacheSection4bModifiedSet), 7 workflow-skills SKILL.md (skillMdModifiedByUs), and 4 replit-deck example decks (exampleHtmlModifiedByUs). craft/ contributes zero — its §4(b) set is empty. design-skills/ is MIT and out of scope for §4(b) entirely. An earlier value of 40 in this entry was never derived and did not match any list in this file; 23 is the sum of the three lists it points at.

resolvedContentDefects.finding: Each declares a Text token and a Surface token, and its own prose instructs pairing them — bold says 'Keep body copy on Text (#111827) for legibility' while 'Use Surface (#111111) for large backgrounds'. Measured WCAG AA contrast before the fix: bold 1.06:1, pacman 1.18:1, energetic 2.11:1, mono 3.82:1. AA requires 4.5:1 for body text, so an agent following the file produced unreadable output.
resolvedContentDefects.fourthFileFoundByTheGate: mono was NOT in the original hand-measured set of three. It was found by scripts/lint-design-systems.mjs on its first run over the corpus — Text #78716B (stone-500) on Surface #E7E5E4 (stone-200) at 3.82:1, the same generator defect in a less obvious form. It is recorded separately because it is the first evidence this gate finds anything a careful manual pass missed.
resolvedContentDefects.cause: Upstream generator defect, not ours. All four came in with the 57-file Schema-B batch from nexu-io/open-design: the dark themes (bold, pacman) kept the light-theme Text default #111827, energetic set Text to a near-copy of its own Primary (#EA580C against Primary #EA580B), and mono picked a mid-ramp grey against a light surface. Verified against our vendored bytes, so re-vendoring may or may not carry the fix.
resolvedContentDefects.detectedBy: Originally, manual WCAG computation over the declared Text/Surface pair, prompted by the google-labs-code/design.md review. Now checked on every run by scripts/lint-design-systems.mjs, wired into `npm run design:systems-lint` and into `npm run verify` after design:html-gate.
resolvedContentDefects.fix: Only the Text token changed, in two places per file (the token bullet and the 'Keep body copy on Text (#…)' prose line). No other byte was touched, so each file remains diffable against upstream at every other line.

fixValues.reasoning: Dark surface. #FAFAFA is not an invention: it is the Text token this same generator emits for the other dark-surface systems in this batch (dashboard and dramatic both declare Text #FAFAFA on Surface #09090B). Using the batch's own correct dark-theme output is the smallest change that fixes the defect without introducing a value the pack does not already use. bold's stated identity is 'high-contrast colors', which 18.09:1 serves and 1.06:1 contradicted.

Same dark-surface rule and same source value as bold. The in-file alternative was Secondary #F4B9B0 (12.41:1, and a genuine arcade colour), but promoting Secondary to body text collapses two roles into one and the file's own Anti-patterns section forbids flattening hierarchy. #FAFAFA leaves every other token's role intact.

Light surface. #111827 is the Text token 34 of the 57 Schema-B files already declare against light surfaces, so it is this batch's own light-theme default. Nothing in energetic's own vocabulary reaches AA against #FDBA74 — the darkest in-file candidate, Danger #DC2626, manages only 2.86:1 — so an in-file value was not available. A warm near-black (orange-950 #431407, 9.28:1) would have been more on-brand but is a value the pack uses nowhere, and inventing one to fix a defect is a design change, not a repair.

Light surface, same rule and same value as energetic. #78716B and #E7E5E4 are stone-500 and stone-200 from one ramp, two steps apart — the file's high-contrast, 'matrix-inspired' stated intent is served by the batch default, not by a mid-ramp grey.

resolvedContentDefects.whyNotAllowlisted: An allowlist would have kept four files shipping prose that promises legibility while producing 1.06:1. Editing vendored bytes does cost byte-comparability against upstream, which is why each file is now in modifiedByUs and apacheSection4bModifiedSet (Apache-2.0 §4(b)) and why the diff is confined to one token per file.
resolvedContentDefects.notFixedHere: The cross-produced role-bucket contrast check was measured at 52.4% false positives (3114 pairs, 1633 below AA) and is deliberately NOT implemented; see the header comment in scripts/lint-design-systems.mjs. Accent-on-surface below 3:1 is reported as a NOTE on 14 files and deliberately does not fail the gate — those are brand primaries on non-text fills, an upstream design choice rather than a defect.
resolvedContentDefects.upstreamStillAffected: Yes. The fix here is local; upstream's generator still emits these defaults. If this pack is re-vendored at a newer sha, re-check these four slugs before assuming the fix survived — the gate will catch it either way.

reVendorRecheck.action: All four files were KEPT at our values and not overwritten. This was the single highest-risk step of the re-vendor: a naive overwrite of the subtree would have silently reintroduced 1.06:1 body text into shipped content, and the four files are otherwise byte-identical to upstream so nothing else about them would have looked wrong.
reVendorRecheck.alsoConfirmed: Upstream changed NOTHING ELSE in any of the four files since our vendoring — identical line counts, and the only differing lines are the two per file that the fix touched. So keeping our version costs no upstream content, and the `fix` field's claim that the diff is confined to one token in two places per file still holds exactly against the pin.
reVendorRecheck.newBrandsChecked: The 14 brands added at this re-vendor were checked for the same defect before landing. None carries a declared Text/Surface pair, so none can carry this defect; see subtrees[design-systems/].newBrands2026-08-03.generatorDefectCheck. No new repair was needed and none was invented.

resolvedContentDefects.status: fixed here 2026-08-14; still present upstream at the pinned sha e1c277c5
resolvedContentDefects.finding: The one file in this pack named after Material described a design system that is not Material. Primary was #6442D6 and Secondary #C8B3FD (Material's are #1976D2 and #9C27B0); the semantic trio was the Tailwind-adjacent #16A34A / #D97706 / #DC2626 rather than Material's #2E7D32 / #ED6C02 / #D32F2F; the body font was Inter while Material specifies Roboto throughout; and the type scale read 12/14/16/20/24/32, which is a six-step generic ramp rather than Material's thirteen named variants (96/60/48/34/24/20/16/14/12, each carrying its own line-height and letter-spacing). The spacing scale 4/8/12/16/24/32 likewise is not the single 8px base unit Material multiplies. An agent handed this file produced output that was not Material in any respect a reader would recognise, while being told it was.
resolvedContentDefects.whyThisIsADefectAndNotAStyleChoice: Every other design-systems/ file is a descriptive analysis of a brand's publicly observable visual language, and the whole subtree's value rests on those descriptions being accurate. A brand file may legitimately simplify or abstract; it may not assert token values the brand does not use. The test applied was not `is this pretty` but `would a reader who knows Material recognise it`, and the answer was no.
resolvedContentDefects.cause: Upstream generator defect, not ours, and NOT the same defect as the Schema-B batch's contrast bug. Two of the wrong values are unique to this file across all 151: #6442D6 appears nowhere else, and `primary=Inter, display=Roboto` appears nowhere else. The generator therefore had some brand-specific signal - it knew Material's display face is Roboto, and it picked a purple in the neighbourhood of Material 3's #6750A4 - but resolved it into a body font and a primary that match neither M2 nor M3. The type scale 12/14/16/20/24/32 is the opposite case: 22 of the 151 files carry it, so that line is a shared generator default that was never specialised for this brand.
resolvedContentDefects.detectedBy: Manual review on 2026-08-14 against mui/material-ui, prompted by a general survey of that repository for material worth adopting. No gate in this pack would have caught it: design:systems-lint checks that a file's declared Text/Surface pair clears WCAG AA and that its sections are in a shipped order, both of which this file passed before and after the fix. Brand ACCURACY is unchecked by construction - there is no machine-readable ground truth for 150 of the 151 brands - and this entry is the record that the gap is known rather than overlooked.
resolvedContentDefects.fix: Values corrected in place, in the five sections that carried them (Color, Typography, Spacing & Grid, Components, Motion & Interaction). Section headings, section order and the Schema-B declared-pair prose lines were preserved, so the file still lints as Schema B and every unchanged line stays diffable against upstream. Sections 1, 5, 8 and 9 were not touched.

fixValues.readFrom: createPalette.js getDefaultWarning(), light mode. Not a ramp value: MUI's own comment reads 'closest to orange[800] that pass 3:1', which is itself an accessibility fix worth preserving rather than rounding to orange[800].

createPalette.js light.text.primary = rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.87). Composited over the declared Surface #FFFFFF that is 255 * 0.13 = 33.15 per channel, i.e. #212121, which is independently grey[900]. An opaque hex was required because the declared-pair contrast check in scripts/lint-design-systems.mjs parses hex only; the substitution is exact rather than approximate, and is recorded here because the file now states a value that does not appear literally in MUI's source.
fixValues.ratioNote: This fix LOWERS contrast, by 1.64, and is the first entry in this file where that is true - every fix under `declared-text-on-surface-contrast` raised it. Stated plainly rather than buried: the change was made for brand accuracy, not accessibility, and 16.1:1 against the 4.5:1 AA floor leaves the margin untouched in any practical sense. design:systems-lint was green before and after, and material appears in neither the failure list nor the accent NOTE list on either side of the change.

fixValues.readFrom: createPalette.js light.background.default/.paper = common.white. UNCHANGED - the one colour token the generator had right.

resolvedContentDefects.nonColourFixes: Typography: scale, families, weights and the full thirteen-variant table (size / weight / line-height / letter-spacing) from createTypography.js, plus its two non-obvious behaviours - base fontSize is 14 against htmlFontSize 16, and MUI drops the letter-spacing entirely when fontFamily is overridden because Roboto's tracking degrades other faces. Spacing: the 8px base unit from createSpacing.ts, borderRadius 4 from shape.ts, and the xs/sm/md/lg/xl 0/600/900/1200/1536 breakpoints from createBreakpoints.ts. Motion: the five durations, the entering/leaving asymmetry, the four easing curves from createTransitions.js, and the light/dark interaction-state opacities from createPalette.js.
resolvedContentDefects.deliberatelyAddedWarnings: Two cross-references were added to the file rather than left implicit, because both are mistakes this pack's own craft files already lint. (1) The motion tokens are M2 and are labelled as such, since craft/animation-discipline.md lints shipping cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) under the name M3. (2) Material's `button` variant is uppercase at 0.02857em tracking, which is below the 0.06em floor craft/typography.md sets for ALL CAPS; the file now says so, so that a brand value is not read as a licence to ignore a craft rule.
resolvedContentDefects.notFixed: The file remains grounded in Material 2 by way of MUI, because that is the source that was actually read. It is not re-grounded on Material 3, whose baseline primary is a different purple again. Section 1's prose still says 'dynamic theming', which is an M3 concept sitting on an M2 token set - left as upstream wrote it rather than rewritten, since resolving it properly means grounding the whole file on M3 and that is separate work against a source this audit did not read.

settledDecisions.decision: central record in this manifest, no per-file headers
settledDecisions.rationale: Per-file notices would destroy byte-comparability against upstream for exactly the files where knowing what we changed matters most. That comparability is how modifiedByUs was reconstructed at all (see separationMethod) and how a future re-vendor tells our edits from upstream drift. The manifest is the pack's documented provenance surface, which is a defensible reading of section 4(b)'s 'prominent notices'.

settledDecisions.decision: no explicit statement added; exposure left as inherited from upstream
settledDecisions.rationale: Considered and declined, deliberately — this is not an oversight. The content is prose analysis of publicly observable visual language, not redistributed brand assets, and the risk profile is unchanged from upstream's. Recorded here so a future audit finds a decision rather than a silence.

settledDecisions.decision: reported as NOTE, never fails the gate
settledDecisions.rationale: A brand primary is normally a CTA fill, which is non-text, so 3:1 is advisory. Failing would red-line vendored brands for expressing their actual identity — the noisy-gate failure mode the defect register already records. Distinct from the four body-text defects, which were genuinely unreadable and were repaired.

settledDecisions.decision: design-systems/ only, pinned; workflow-skills/ left at the window
settledDecisions.rationale: The cheaper and better half: it brought 14 new brands and realigned 7 upstream-drifted files, at one subtree, with the 12 local edits verified surviving. The workflow-skills half is mostly deck-skin variants and would have put all remaining local edits at risk in the same operation.
